findings.breaking_input: A row whose adapter fetches a URL on the venture domain that answers 302 with Location to an allowed vendor host or a host under a shared suffix. The prior redirect defect was fixed for ctx.fetch elsewhere, but resolveHosts widens the allow-list to brand.domain and every subdomain, so a venture domain with an open redirect or a dangling subdomain (a CNAME to a deprovisioned vercel.app or herokuapp.com project) is a reachable host that is not the venture's.
findings.why: hostAllowed admits every subdomain of brand.domain. A subdomain takeover on dangling.myfitfolio.com is inside the allow-list, so a credentialed fetch (a GitHub or Vercel token header) can be sent to an attacker-controlled server. The allow-list was a fixed literal before, and now it is data the venture owner controls.
findings.fix: For rows that carry credential headers, do not allow the @venture subtree for authenticated calls: allow the apex and the www label only, or strip Authorization on any host that is not a vendor literal.
findings.twin_of: ctx.fetch checked only the first URL and let `fetch` follow redirects to a host nobody checked -> every allowlist checked once on an input that the callee may replace (redirects, retries, resolved names)

findings.breaking_input: brand.domain = `ltd.uk` fits CC_SECOND_LEVEL and is refused, but `sch.uk`, `nom.es`, `ac.in`-style names outside the list, `gov.au`'s `edu.au`, `co.jp`'s sibling `ne.jp`, `or.jp`, `go.kr`, `or.kr`, `com.br`, `net.br` (br is two letters, and com/net are in the list) resolve. `ne.jp`, `or.jp`, `go.jp`, `co.id`-style entries: `or.jp`, `ne.jp`, `sch.uk` are not matched. `ne.jp` passes BARE_HOST, is not in MULTI_TENANT, and is not matched by CC_SECOND_LEVEL.
findings.why: A closed hand-picked list is the same defect the lane just recorded as fixed. Round 1 widened it by a handful of names, and a domain that is one registry suffix is admitted with every registrant under it.
findings.fix: Treat any two-label name whose first label is 1-3 letters and whose last label is a two-letter ccTLD as a shared suffix, and add ne, or, go, sch, nom, mil, gob. A real venture on a ccTLD uses three labels or one label above a known TLD.
findings.twin_of: The shared-suffix list was a handful of names -> one list in `public-suffixes.mjs` read by ctx and lint; the row's own literals always join the collision set

findings.breaking_input: The first apply exits 1 and the failure reason is written by an adapter: `reason` starts with `refused:` only if the runner writes that prefix. An adapter whose scaffold throws an Error with message `refused: x` and code undefined is recorded as `failed` with reason built from adapter text. Conversely, an adapter that fails with a reason not starting `refused:` after creating a resource (a provider timeout after the POST) is retried at once.
findings.why: The retry decision branches on free text in `reason`. The lane's own rule is that a free-text prefix choosing the outcome is a defect when the text is adapter-controlled. An adapter can force a retry or suppress one by choosing its words, and a retry re-runs a scaffold whose first attempt may have half-created a resource.
findings.fix: Branch on a field the runner sets from a closed set (reason_code or a refused flag written by the runner), not on adapter text; and keep the retry only for a runner-classified timeout.
findings.twin_of: A free-text reason prefix (`env:`) chose the outcome -> every branch on adapter text: is the text adapter-controlled?

findings.breaking_input: A real venture where a slot is `absent` from an earlier apply and a later slot exists: the walk stops with exit 2 at the absent slot. A rehearsal with the same board passes it over, and the order.find also treats a slot in state `failed`, `awaiting` or `running` as the next one.
findings.why: A slot stuck in `running` because another process crashed holding it is picked and apply() decides. But the walk reads state before apply() takes the lock, so two walks started together both pick the same slot, and the loser stops with exit 3. A walk that finds `applying` left by a killed runner has no stale-lock handling of its own.
findings.fix: Document and test that a walk is single-writer, or take the venture lock around the whole select-and-apply step.
findings.twin_of: Gate check-then-emit ran outside the lock, so two applies made two requests -> every check-then-act on shared state

findings.breaking_input: A file `x.venture.yaml` that is a symlink to a regular file: lstatSync(...).isFile() is false for a link, so it is reported. A file whose YAML `slug:` differs from the name (`a.venture.yaml` holding `slug: b`) loads by the file-derived name, so the lint checks it while the runner selects by slug.
findings.why: The B7 fix covered the directory and link cases only. The slug-vs-filename mismatch from the earlier finding was left open, so the lint can judge a profile under a name no run will use.
findings.fix: After loadProfile, assert profile.slug === slug and add a finding when they differ.
findings.twin_of: The adapter path was data the runner trusted

findings.breaking_input: An apply() that prints adapter words through `log` before the final line: `last` is cleaned only in the closing stopped-at line, but the same string is printed raw by `log` one line earlier (`console.log(line)`), so a reason holding a newline plus a fake `walk complete: 9 applied, 0 skipped` still reaches the terminal.
findings.why: The fix cleaned the second print and left the first. Any consumer parsing stdout for the `walk complete` line can be forged.
findings.fix: Have `log` print clean(line), or print only through one cleaned path.
findings.twin_of: Adapter-supplied strings (resource ids, reasons, answerers) were printed raw, so a newline or escape could forge a line -> every terminal line that interpolates provider or adapter data
